T: Easter with the whole Filipino family.
D: A struggling comedian heads home for a chaotic Filipino-American family Easter with his mum and aunties.
P: Serve the main when the whole family sits down for Easter lunch.
S: Crisp Filipino spring rolls filled with pork and vegetables, with sweet chilli for dipping. Mix 500g pork mince with grated carrot, onion, garlic and soy.
Stir-fried noodles with chicken and vegetables, the noodle dish at every Filipino party. Soak 250g rice vermicelli.
M: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy, garlic and bay leaves, served with plenty of rice. Brown 1kg chicken thighs.
W: Silky caramel custard flan, the Filipino party dessert. Melt 150g sugar to a caramel and pour into a dish.
K: Lime and lemon juice with sparkling water over ice.

s.how: Mix 500g pork mince with grated carrot, onion, garlic and soy. Roll tightly in 20 spring roll wrappers and fry at 180C until golden. Serve with sweet chilli sauce.
Soak 250g rice vermicelli. Stir-fry 300g sliced chicken with garlic, carrot and cabbage, add 3 tbsp soy and 250ml stock, then toss through the noodles. Serve with lemon wedges.

m.how: Brown 1kg chicken thighs. Add 120ml vinegar, 80ml soy, 6 garlic cloves, 3 bay leaves and pepper and simmer covered 35 minutes. Reduce the sauce and serve with 300g jasmine rice.

w.how: Melt 150g sugar to a caramel and pour into a dish. Whisk 6 egg yolks with 395g condensed milk and 370ml evaporated milk, pour in and bake in a water bath at 160C for 50 minutes. Chill and turn out.

d.how: Mix the juice of 4 limes and 2 lemons with 4 tbsp sugar until dissolved. Top with 1L sparkling water and serve over ice. Make it just before the film starts and keep the jug cold.
